adapt: Use one high-signal community promise as the entry point instead of stacking multiple marketing sections above the fold.
Let real event or portfolio evidence enter the viewport early without competing with the primary message.
Preserve hierarchy across breakpoints even when navigation changes orientation.
reject: Do not reuse the event artwork, identity, copy, or exact typographic scale and spacing.
Do not infer event-card interaction, ticketing behavior, or accessibility from static captures.
The user must immediately operate controls, compare records, or complete a transactional workflow.

adapt: Demonstrate a mobile product inside its native device context before relying on explanatory copy.
Use a small number of social fragments to establish emotional context around concrete product proof.
Reduce decorative fragments and strengthen the direct acquisition action on mobile.
reject: Do not reuse user photos, stickers, interface screens, identity, copy, or exact device composition.
Do not infer retention, sharing behavior, privacy, or app performance from the landing page.
The target is a desktop operational product or the device mockup would obscure the primary workflow.
